chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khallid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man is in the desert of the earth on a cloudy day, so he prays facing a direction other than the Qiblah. Then morning comes and he realizes that he had prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah. What should he do?' He said: 'If it is still within the prayer time, let him repeat his prayer; and if the time has passed, his effort (of determining the direction) is sufficient for him.'

key_terms.يَوْمِ غَيْمٍ: cloudy day (obscuring the sun/stars for direction)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a prayer performed in the desert if one later realizes they faced the wrong direction?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ijtihad* in prayer direction (*qiblah*) for those in remote areas, distinguishing between cases where the error is rectifiable within the prayer window and those where it is not. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness, absolving the worshipper of fault when they have exerted due diligence in determining the Qiblah under difficult conditions like cloud cover. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, ensuring that religious obligations remain accessible even when precise orientation is challenging.
